Unconsolidated Joint Venture The Company owns a 20% equity interest in one Unconsolidated Joint Venture which, as of June 30, 2026, owned a portfolio of six properties with an aggregate of 1.0 million leasable square feet located in six states. All assets in the joint venture portfolio are performing and the portfolio has an Occupancy Rate of 100% with a Weighted Average Remaining Lease Term of 5.8 years as of June 30, 2026. The Company has also made a member loan to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture (the “Member Loan”) with an outstanding principal balance of $5.5 million as of June 30, 2026. As previously disclosed, the non-recourse mortgage notes associated with the Unconsolidated Joint Venture, which had an outstanding principal balance of $125.6 million as of August 6, 2026, experienced a payment default at maturity in February 2026. The lenders’ agent under the loan has issued a default notice and has informed the joint venture that it intends to seek to compel a sale of the properties in the joint venture in order to repay the loan. During June 2026, the lenders agreed to extend the loan maturity date until July 31, 2026, to provide the Unconsolidated Joint Venture with time to consummate the sale of one of the six properties, however the sale transaction was subsequently terminated and the loan went back into default on August 1, 2026. The lenders have implemented an excess cash flow sweep and as a result of the loan default, have various additional rights and remedies that are customary in a non-recourse mortgage financing, such as the right to collect default interest, institute a proceeding for foreclosure and apply for the appointment of a receiver. The joint venture has delivered a proposed disposition strategy to the lenders for the six properties and remains in discussions with the lenders about next steps which may include a short-term extension and the requirement to sell one or more properties and utilize the proceeds to repay principal outstanding under the debt. The Company cannot provide any assurance that the Unconsolidated Joint Venture will be able to extend or refinance all or any portion of this debt obligation, complete the disposition of the six properties on favorable terms or in a timely manner, or at all, or that the lenders will not seek to enforce their remedies due to the ongoing payment default. Due to uncertainties with regard to the recovery of its investments in the Unconsolidated Joint Venture, the Company reduced the carrying value of its investment in the Unconsolidated Joint Venture to zero as of December 31, 2025, and has recorded a loan loss reserve for the entire outstanding principal balance of its Member Loan. The Company accounts for its investment in the Unconsolidated Joint Venture under the equity method of accounting and during the year ended December 31, 2025, its share of losses exceeded the carrying amount of its investment. Accordingly, the Company has suspended recognition of its share of additional losses and will resume recognizing its share of earnings only after the Unconsolidated Joint Venture generates net income that exceeds the previously recognized losses. The Company has not recognized any further losses in excess of its investment and no contingent liabilities have been recorded related to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture as of and for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026. Additionally, beginning January 1, 2026, the Company is recording management fees from the Unconsolidated Joint Venture and interest income on the Member Loan on a cash basis rather than an accrual basis. Historically, the Company has included its proportionate share of the Unconsolidated Joint Venture's financial statement line items and operating metrics in its non-GAAP financial results and other operating metrics. This includes, among other line items and metrics, the Company’s proportionate share of Annualized Base Rent, Occupied Square Feet, Rentable Square Feet and Weighted Average Remaining Lease Term from the Unconsolidated Joint Venture properties, and Gross Real Estate Investments, outstanding principal balance under debt obligations, cash and cash equivalents, and restricted cash from the Unconsolidated Joint Venture’s balance sheet. As a result of the factors described above, including the suspension of equity method accounting on the Unconsolidated Joint Venture, the full loan loss reserve recorded against its Member Loan and the recording of fees and interest income on a cash basis, beginning January 1, 2026, the Company no longer includes the proportionate share of the Unconsolidated Joint Venture’s financial statement line items and operating metrics in its non-GAAP financial results and other operating metrics. Definitions Annualized Base Rent ("ABR") is the monthly aggregate cash amount charged to tenants under our leases (including monthly base rent receivables and certain fixed contractually obligated reimbursements by our tenants), as of the final date of the applicable period, multiplied by 12. Annualized Base Rent is not indicative of future performance. Dedicated Use Asset is a property that includes a substantial specialized use component such as government, medical, laboratory and research and development, and flex operations, and would therefore not be considered a traditional office property. Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization for Real Estate ("EBITDAre") and Adjusted EBITDA Due to certain unique operating characteristics of real estate companies, as discussed below, the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts, Inc. ("Nareit"), an industry trade group, has promulgated a supplemental performance measure known as Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization for Real Estate. Nareit defines EBITDAre as net income (loss) computed in accordance with GAAP, adjusted for interest expense, income tax expense (benefit), depreciation and amortization, impairment write-downs on real estate and investments in entities when the impairment is directly attributable to decreases in the value of depreciable real estate held by the entity, gains or losses from disposition of real estate assets. For periods prior to January 1, 2026, we also adjust for our proportionate share of EBITDAre adjustments related to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture. We calculated EBITDAre in accordance with Nareit's definition described above. In addition to EBITDAre, we use Adjusted EBITDA as a non-GAAP supplemental performance measure to evaluate the operating performance of the Company. Adjusted EBITDA, as defined by the Company, represents EBITDAre, modified to exclude non-routine items such as transaction related expenses. We also exclude certain non-cash items such as impairments of intangible and right of use assets, gains or losses on derivatives, gains or losses on the extinguishment or forgiveness of debt, amortization of intangibles, above-market lease assets and deferred lease incentives, net of amortization of below-market lease liabilities and, for periods prior to January 1, 2026, our proportionate share of Adjusted EBITDA adjustments related to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture. Management believes that excluding these costs from EBITDAre provides investors with supplemental performance information that is consistent with the performance models and analysis used by management, and provides investors a view of the performance of our portfolio over time. Therefore, EBITDAre and Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss), as determined under GAAP. The Company uses Adjusted EBITDA as one measure of its operating performance when formulating corporate goals and evaluating the effectiveness of the Company's strategies. EBITDAre and Adjusted EBITDA may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. Funds Available for Distribution ("FAD") Funds available for distribution, as defined by the Company, represents Core FFO, as defined below, modified to exclude capital expenditures and leasing costs, as well as certain non-cash items such as amortization of above market leases, net of amortization of below market lease liabilities, straight-line rental revenue, and, for periods prior to January 1, 2026, our proportionate share of FAD adjustments related to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture and amortization of the Unconsolidated Joint Venture basis difference. Management believes that adjusting these items from Core FFO provides investors with supplemental performance information that is consistent with the performance models and analysis used by management and provides useful information regarding the Company's ability to fund its dividend. However, not all REITs calculate FAD and those that do may not calculate FAD the same way, so comparisons with other REITs may not be meaningful. FAD should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or cash flow provided by (used in) operating activities as determined under GAAP. Nareit Funds from Operations ("Nareit FFO" or "FFO") and Core Funds from Operations ("Core FFO") Due to certain unique operating characteristics of real estate companies, as discussed below, Nareit has promulgated a supplemental performance measure known as FFO, which we believe to be an appropriate supplemental performance measure to reflect the operating performance of the Company. FFO is not equivalent to our net income (loss) as determined under GAAP. Nareit defines FFO as net income (loss) computed in accordance with GAAP adjusted for gains or losses from disposition of real estate assets, depreciation and amortization of real estate assets, impairment write-downs on real estate and investments in entities when the impairment is directly attributable to decreases in the value of depreciable real estate held by the entity. For periods prior to January 1, 2026, we also adjust for our proportionate share of FFO adjustments related to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture. We calculate FFO in accordance with Nareit's definition described above. In addition to FFO, we use Core FFO as a non-GAAP supplemental financial performance measure to evaluate the operating performance of the Company. Core FFO, as defined by the Company, excludes from FFO items that we believe do not reflect the ongoing operating performance of our business such as transaction related expenses, amortization of deferred financing costs, amortization of deferred lease incentives, net, equity-based compensation, amortization of premiums and discounts on debt, net and gains or losses on extinguishment of swaps and/or debt, and, for periods prior to January 1, 2026, our proportionate share of Core FFO adjustments related to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture. We believe that FFO and Core FFO allow for a comparison of the performance of our operations with other publicly-traded REITs, as FFO and Core FFO, or a substantially similar measure, are routinely reported by publicly-traded REITs, each adjust for items that we believe do not reflect the ongoing operating performance of our business and we believe are often used by analysts and investors for comparison purposes. For all of these reasons, we believe FFO and Core FFO, in addition to net income (loss), as determined under GAAP, are helpful supplemental performance measures and useful in understanding the various ways in which our management evaluates the performance of the Company over time. However, not all REITs calculate FFO and Core FFO the same way, so comparisons with other REITs may not be meaningful. FFO and Core FFO should not be considered as alternatives to net income (loss) and are not intended to be used as a liquidity measure indicative of cash flow available to fund our cash needs. Neither the SEC, Nareit, nor any other regulatory body has evaluated the acceptability of the exclusions used to adjust FFO in order to calculate Core FFO and its use as a non-GAAP financial performance measure. Net Debt, Principal Outstanding and Adjusted Principal Outstanding Principal Outstanding is a non-GAAP measure that represents the Company's outstanding principal debt balance, excluding certain GAAP adjustments, such as premiums and discounts, financing and issuance costs, and related accumulated amortization. For periods prior to January 1, 2026, Adjusted Principal Outstanding includes the Company's proportionate share of the Unconsolidated Joint Venture's outstanding principal debt balance. We believe that the presentation of Principal Outstanding and Adjusted Principal Outstanding, which show our contractual debt obligations, provides useful information to investors to assess our overall financial flexibility, capital structure and leverage. Principal Outstanding and Adjusted Principal Outstanding should not be considered as alternatives to the Company's consolidated debt balance as determined under GAAP or any other GAAP financial measures and should only be considered together with, and as a supplement to, the Company's financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Net Debt is a non-GAAP measure used to show the Company's Adjusted Principal Outstanding, less all cash and cash equivalents and, for periods prior to January 1, 2026, the Company's proportionate share of the Unconsolidated Joint Venture's cash and cash equivalents. Beginning January 1, 2026, the Company has revised its definition and calculation of Net Debt to also add restricted cash to the amounts that reduce the Company’s Adjusted Principal Outstanding under debt obligations. This change in definition has also been applied retrospectively for comparison purposes and, for periods prior to January 1, 2026, also includes the Company’s proportionate share of restricted cash from the Unconsolidated Joint Venture. We believe that the presentation of Net Debt provides useful information to investors because our management reviews Net Debt as part of its management of our overall liquidity, financial flexibility, capital structure and leverage. Net Operating Income ("NOI"), Cash NOI, Trailing NOI and Trailing Cash NOI NOI is a non-GAAP performance measure used to evaluate the operating performance of a real estate company. NOI represents total revenues less property operating expenses and excludes fee revenue earned for services to the Unconsolidated Joint Venture, impairment, depreciation and amortization, general and administrative expenses, and transaction related expenses. Cash NOI excludes the impact of certain GAAP adjustments included in rental revenue, such as straight-line rental revenue, amortization of above-market intangible lease assets and below-market lease intangible liabilities, and amortization of deferred lease incentives. For periods prior to January 1, 2026, Cash NOI includes the proportionate share of such amounts from properties owned by the Unconsolidated Joint Venture. Trailing NOI and Trailing Cash NOI represent trailing 12-month NOI and Cash NOI, calculated for the most recent 12-month period as of the applicable date. It is management's view that NOI and Cash NOI provide investors relevant and useful information because it reflects only income and operating expense items that are incurred at the property level and presents them on an unleveraged basis. NOI and Cash NOI should not be considered as an alternative to operating income in accordance with GAAP. Further, NOI and Cash NOI may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. title: 7 Best Google Slides Alternatives I Tested in 2026
summary: I tested dozens of Google Slides alternatives and found the 7 best options for design, AI slide generation, offline work, and brand control in 2026.
body_text: August 12th, 2026 7 Best Google Slides Alternatives I Tested in 2026 By Tyler Shibata · 23 min read X LinkedIn I spent the last few weeks testing Google Slides alternatives on work decks, from investor updates to sales pitches. Canva, PowerPoint, and Beautiful.ai came out ahead after I compared over 20 options for design control, AI slide generation, and speed. Here are the 7 tools worth switching to in 2026, plus the one situation where Google Slides still holds up. 7 best Google Slides alternatives: TL;DR Canva : Best for non-designers who want free, polished slides fast. Microsoft PowerPoint : Best for offline work and the Microsoft ecosystem. Beautiful.ai : Best for auto-formatted, on-brand business decks. Julius : Best for marketers and analysts turning data analysis into slide-ready decks. Pitch : Best for collaborative, design-forward team decks. Gamma : Best for AI-generated first drafts from a prompt. Prezi : Best for non-linear, zoomable storytelling. Why look for Google Slides alternatives? I'll give Google Slides credit where it's due. It's free, opens in any browser, and lets your whole team edit the same deck at once . That convenience is why so many teams default to it for a quick update. Presentation software is also a crowded, growing category. It's projected to more than double from $8.6 billion in 2026 to over $21 billion by 2033, according to Coherent Market Insights , so you've got plenty of alternatives if Slides doesn't fit the job in front of you. That said, once I started pushing Slides on decks that mattered, a handful of gaps kept showing up: The design ceiling shows up fast: Templates work fine for an internal update and fall flat in front of a client. Getting a deck to stand out takes manual work Google Slides doesn't help with. Brand control is loose: You can share a theme, but anyone on the team can override it. Without a true brand lock, fonts and colors drift the more people touch a deck. Native AI is thin: Native AI has improved, but it still may not match the depth of specialized AI presentation tools for teams that want more control over branding, storytelling, or automation. Offline access takes setup ahead of time: You need to enable offline mode in Google Drive and use Chrome or Edge with the Google Docs Offline extension before you lose your connection. It stays tied to Google's ecosystem: You need a Google account, and core Slides editing still centers on Google’s web tools, which can be a dealbreaker if you’re trying to move off Google or work on a locked-down machine. Which Google Slides alternative should you choose? The right Google Slides alternative depends on how much design help you want, whether your deck starts with data or a blank page, and how much your team cares about staying on-brand. Choose: Canva if you want free, polished slides without any design background. Stronger brand controls sit behind Canva's paid plans. Microsoft PowerPoint if your team already works inside the Microsoft ecosystem and needs a deck to work without wifi. The interface can feel more complex if you're used to editing in a browser tab. Beautiful.ai if you want decks to stay on-brand automatically as different people build them. You give up some layout freedom to get that consistency. Julius if your presentation comes out of data you still need to analyze. You can build charts straight into a slide-ready deck, though the template selection is smaller than some of the dedicated design tools on this list. Pitch if your team builds decks together in real time and wants better visibility into collaboration and edits. AI features run on a credit system, and the Free plan only gets a one-time allocation to start. Gamma if you want a full first draft built from one prompt. Plan on polishing the output before it goes in front of a client. Prezi if your presentation tells a story that benefits from zooming and movement. That same format can feel busy for a straightforward business update. Stick with Google Slides if real-time collaboration matters more than design polish, and everyone on your team already lives in Google Drive. 7 best Google Slides alternatives: At a glance 💻 Tool 🎯 Best for 🔥 Starting price (billed annually) Canva Free, polished slides without design skills $180/year Microsoft PowerPoint Offline work in the Microsoft ecosystem $99.99/year Microsoft 365 subscription (or $179.99 one-time purchase) Beautiful.ai Decks that stay on brand automatically $12/month Julius Presentations built from your own data analysis $16/month Pitch Real time collaboration with edit tracking $13/month Gamma A full deck draft from one prompt $9/seat/month Prezi Zooming, non-linear storytelling $7/month *Pricing correct as of August 2026. Verify with vendor. 1. Canva: Best for free, polished slides without design skills Canva is a design platform with a presentation editor built in, along with tools for social graphics, documents, and video. The template library covers most industries and use cases , so a deck rarely starts from a blank slide. Leaning too heavily on a single template can leave a deck looking close to what other users have already published. Key features Template library: Offers thousands of presentation templates, filtered by style, industry, and use case. Magic Design: Generates a draft deck from a text prompt. Brand hub: Stores logos, fonts, and colors to keep presentations on-brand, with more brand-management capacity on paid plans. Pros ✅ Includes a free plan with presentation creation and limited AI features ✅ Combines slides, social posts, and other marketing assets in one editor ✅ Supports real-time collaboration with comments and task assignment Cons ❌ Rely too heavily on templates and a deck can look close to everyone else's ❌ Shift layouts and formatting when exported to PowerPoint, so cleanup is often needed Best for Marketers who want polished slides without a design background Teams that already use Canva for other content and want one tool for everything Non-designers who need a deck finished fast Pricing Canva starts at $144 per year . 2. Microsoft PowerPoint: Best for offline work and the Microsoft ecosystem PowerPoint is Microsoft's presentation software, available as a desktop app with a web version for cloud collaboration . It offers full offline access and deep design control, along with native integration with Teams, OneDrive, and the rest of Microsoft 365. Real-time co-editing lags behind cloud-native tools, and version conflicts can still happen. Key features Full design toolkit: Includes animations, transitions, and precise control over every element. Copilot AI: Drafts slides, summarizes documents, and rewrites text inside the app. Ecosystem integrations: Links natively to Teams, OneDrive, and the rest of Microsoft 365. Pros ✅ Provides a true offline desktop app, plus a web version for collaboration ✅ Offers the most complete feature set of any tool on this list ✅ Speeds up first drafts and text cleanup with Copilot Cons ❌ Real-time co-editing works best when files are saved in OneDrive or SharePoint, and version conflicts can still happen in shared workflows ❌ Brand consistency still depends a lot on templates and team habits unless you are using Microsoft’s newer Brand kit and Copilot workflows Best for Teams that need real offline access for decks Companies already running on Microsoft 365 Users who want the most advanced design controls in a slide tool Pricing PowerPoint starts at $99.99 per year as part of a Microsoft 365 subscription, or $179.99 as a one-time purchase . 3. Beautiful.ai: Best for auto-formatted, on-brand business decks Beautiful.ai is a presentation tool that handles the layout decisions for a deck automatically . Its Smart Slides adjust spacing and alignment as content gets added, so even a rushed deck still looks deliberate. That consistency comes at a cost for teams that need precise, freeform control over slide placement. 💡 Tip: Not sold on Beautiful.ai? Check out our Beautiful.ai alternatives guide . Key features Smart Slides: Adjusts formatting automatically as a layout fills with content. AI content generation: Drafts slide text and outlines from a prompt. Brand kit: Applies logos, fonts, and colors across a team's decks. Pros ✅ Keeps a full deck visually consistent without manual tweaking ✅ Includes unlimited AI content generation on paid plans, so teams do not have to manage usage credits ✅ Gives teams with multiple presenters strong brand controls Cons ❌ Feels rigid for anyone who needs precise, manual placement, since the automation runs the layout ❌ Advanced governance, admin controls, and deeper brand guardrails are reserved for Team and Enterprise tiers Best for Business teams that want on-brand decks without freeform design work Teams rebuilding similar proposals or reports on a regular basis Presenters who'd rather trade layout control for consistency Pricing Beautiful.ai starts at $12 per month . Learn more in our Beautiful.ai pricing guide . 4. Julius: Best for presentations built from your own data analysis Julius is an AI-powered data analysis tool that turns your analysis into a slide-ready deck. Ask a question in plain English, and it builds the charts and the presentation from the same analysis , no separate design tool required. The template selection for those decks is smaller than what dedicated design tools offer. Key features Data connectors: Links to sources like Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery, and Google Sheets. Financial Datasets integration : Pulls financial statements, price history, and company metrics for 17,000+ companies. AI presentation maker : Builds slide decks from chat-based analysis, with export to PPT, PDF, or Google Slides. Pros ✅ Skips the step of moving analysis from a spreadsheet into a separate design tool ✅ Covers three ways to get data in: connecting your own sources, searching the web, or pulling company financials ✅ Remembers context and preferences to help work move faster over time Cons ❌ Offers a smaller template library than tools built primarily for slide design ❌ Can return slightly different results on repeat queries, since the underlying analysis isn't always identical run to run Best for Marketers and analysts who need charts and a deck built from the same analysis Teams that want to skip switching between a data tool and a design tool Business users who'd rather start from a question than a blank slide Pricing Julius starts at $16 per month . 5. Pitch: Best for real time collaboration with edit tracking Pitch is a presentation tool built for teams that build decks together. Real-time co-editing, slide assignments, and comments turn a deck into a shared workspace instead of a file passed back and forth. Design customization has a ceiling, so complex, non-standard layouts can feel boxed in. 💡 Tip: Not sold on Pitch? Check out our Pitch alternatives guide . Key features Real-time collaboration: Co-edits, assigns slides, and tracks progress across a team. Engagement analytics: Shows when someone opens a shared deck and which slides hold their attention. Pitch rooms: Shares decks through branded links and dedicated viewing spaces. Pros ✅ Gives teams a collaborative workflow ✅ Includes unlimited presentations on the free plan ✅ Shows engagement data on what's actually landing with viewers Cons ❌ Pitch uses AI credits for AI actions, and workspaces can set a monthly credit budget ❌ Exported decks may not preserve every interactive or web-native Pitch feature when shared as static files Best for Sales and startup teams that build and share decks together Marketing teams that want visibility into who's viewing a deck and when Teams that assign slide ownership and want to track progress in one place Pricing Pitch starts at $13 per month . 6. Gamma: Best for a full deck draft from one prompt Gamma is an AI presentation tool that turns a prompt or outline into a full draft in under a minute. It builds a card-based deck that resizes and reflows on the web , instead of locking to a fixed 16:9 layout. Card layouts do not map cleanly to fixed PowerPoint slides, so exports often need cleanup. 💡 Tip: Not sold on Gamma? Check out our Gamma alternatives guide . Key features Prompt-to-deck generation: Turns a prompt or outline into a full draft automatically. Card-based format: Resizes and reflows web-native slides instead of locking to 16:9. Themes and templates: Applies a look across the whole deck in one click. Pros ✅ Generates a usable first draft quickly, faster than building slide by slide ✅ Looks sharp when shared by link, since the format is built for the web ✅ Includes a free plan that's easy to test before committing Cons ❌ Gamma’s free plan includes 400 one-time AI credits that do not refresh ❌ Exporting to PowerPoint can require cleanup because Gamma’s web-native card layout doesn’tt always translate cleanly to fixed slide formats Best for Anyone who wants a fast first draft built from a single prompt Teams that share decks by link rather than exporting to PowerPoint Users testing AI slide generation before committing to a paid plan Pricing Gamma starts at $9 per seat per month . 7. Prezi: Best for zooming, non-linear storytelling Prezi is a presentation tool built around a single zoomable canvas . Moving between topics with motion, rather than clicking through pages, can make connected ideas easier to follow in a live talk. Overusing the zoom effect can make an audience uncomfortable, and the format isn't built for structured business decks. Key features Zoomable canvas: Moves between topics with motion instead of linear slides. Visual transitions: Includes built-in zoom and pan effects for storytelling. Templates: Offers a library of canvas-based layouts to start from. Pros ✅ Delivers a genuinely different format that stands out in live presentations ✅ Includes a free plan to try the canvas approach ✅ Fits conference talks and narrative-driven pitches well What users say ❌ Comes with a real learning curve, and overusing the zoom can make an audience uncomfortable ❌ Has lighter brand-governance controls than tools built for structured business decks, so it can feel less suited to strict slide-by-slide workflows Best for Presenters who want a visual, non-linear format for live talks Conference speakers building a narrative-driven presentation Anyone moving away from a traditional slide-by-slide structure Pricing Prezi starts at $7 per month . Special mentions These tools didn't make the main list, but each one fits a specific setup depending on your platform and how you feel about staying inside Google's ecosystem. Here are 3 more presentation tools worth a look: Keynote : Apple’s presentation app comes free on Apple devices, and Keynote for iCloud also lets you create, edit, collaborate, and present in a web browser on Mac or Windows. I've found it handles motion and transitions better than most tools on this list, but that polish only travels with you if you're staying inside the Apple ecosystem. Zoho Show : A cloud-based presentation tool that makes the most sense if your team already runs on Zoho apps. In my testing, it felt closer to Google Slides than any other tool here, real-time co-editing included, so switching over doesn't ask your team to relearn much. LibreOffice Impress : LibreOffice Impress is a free, open source presentation editor that’s part of the LibreOffice suite. It works offline with no account required, and I’d point privacy-focused teams here first. I still find the design experience less polished than newer tools like Beautiful.ai or Canva. How to evaluate Google Slides alternatives Picking the right tool here comes down to one honest question. What are you actually building this deck for, and who has to touch it after you? Consider: Design control: Decide upfront how much design freedom you're willing to trade for speed. Beautiful.ai and Gamma will design most of the deck for you, and I've had good and bad experiences with that trade. Good when I'm short on time, frustrating the one time I needed a layout the tool just wouldn't give me. AI generation: Compare a standalone AI tool against the AI add-ons already built into Google Slides before you assume you need something new. A full deck from a single prompt sounds great until you're rewriting half of it anyway. Collaboration and permissions: Check what co-editing actually looks like on the plan you're buying. I've seen teams lose time because plan-level permissions didn't match what they expected. Export fidelity: Test your export before the deck matters, especially if a client's opening the file in PowerPoint. I've had fonts shift and charts resize in ways that only show up once the file leaves the tool it was built in. Offline access: Check whether a tool needs a live connection before you build a deck around it. PowerPoint still works with no connection once it's installed, and I've learned the hard way that most web-based tools need you online just to open one. Substance over polish: Get your analysis and charts right before you worry about how the slide looks. The best-looking deck in the world falls apart if the numbers behind it are wrong. From data to deck in a single tool Finding the right Google Slides alternative solves half the problem. If your presentations are data-heavy, the slowdown usually happens before you open any slide tool, back when you're wrangling the numbers. We built Julius for that part of the work. It connects to your data (or pulls financials for 17,000+ companies through the Financial Datasets integration ), then answers your questions in plain English. From there, it turns those answers into charts you can build into a slide-ready deck , or export to whichever tool you picked above. Ready to build the analysis behind your next deck? Try Julius for free today . Frequently asked questions Is there a better free alternative to Google Slides? Yes, Canva is the strongest free pick, with the most templates and AI features at no cost. Gamma and Pitch also offer free plans if you want AI slide generation or team collaboration without paying. What is the equivalent of Google Slides? The closest equivalents are PowerPoint for the web , Canva Presentations , and Pitch . All three let you create, share, and co-edit decks in a browser. What is the best Google Slides alternative for business teams? Beautiful.ai and PowerPoint are the strongest picks for polished, on-brand business decks. Pitch is the better choice for teams that build and share presentations collaboratively. Can I open Google Slides files in these tools? Yes, in most cases . Export your Slides deck to PowerPoint (.pptx) or PDF first, then import it, and expect minor formatting cleanup, especially with Canva and Gamma. Do any Google Slides alternatives work offline? Yes, PowerPoint works fully offline once it's installed on your desktop. Most web-based tools on this list, including Google Slides, need an internet connection to open or edit a deck.

title: Best CPU for the RTX 5070: Four Contenders, One Clear Winner
summary: We match four CPUs to the RTX 5070 at 1440p. The $329 Ryzen 7 7700X3D wins on cache, price and platform life. Here is the full comparison.
body_text: The RTX 5070 has settled into a comfortable spot in 2026: a 12GB GDDR7 card on a 192-bit bus that is built for high-refresh 1440p gaming, priced from around $642 on Newegg. That makes it the card a lot of people build around this year, which raises the obvious follow-up question. Which processor should sit next to it? Pair a 5070 with too little CPU and the card idles while the processor scrambles to feed it. Pair it with too much and you have spent money that would have been better aimed at storage or memory. Below are four realistic candidates, compared on the things that actually matter for this card, followed by a straight answer. What the RTX 5070 Actually Asks For A 12GB GDDR7 card aimed squarely at high-refresh 1440p. Start with what the card is for. At 1440p with settings turned up, the RTX 5070 is usually the component doing the hardest work, and the processor’s job is to keep the frame pipeline full. But 1440p is also the resolution where CPU limits start to show, particularly in games that simulate a lot at once: large multiplayer maps, strategy titles with hundreds of units, city builders, and simulators. In those cases the deciding factor is not core count. It is memory latency and cache, because the CPU spends its time chasing game-state data rather than crunching through parallel math. That is why cache-heavy processors punch above their specifications in gaming. Current RTX 5070 options on Newegg include the ASUS PRIME RTX 5070 at $641.99, the GIGABYTE Eagle RTX 5070 OC at $659.99, and the GIGABYTE Gaming RTX 5070 OC at $679.99. Whichever you pick, the CPU decision below is the same. Contender 1: Ryzen 7 7700X3D, $329 104MB of total cache is the reason this chip punches above its clock speed in games. The Ryzen 7 7700X3D is a Zen 4 chip with 8 cores and 16 threads, a 4.0 GHz base and 4.5 GHz boost, and 104MB of total cache, of which 96MB is L3 courtesy of AMD’s 3D V-Cache. Its TDP is 120W. On paper the clock speeds look unremarkable next to Intel’s parts, and that is exactly the point of an X3D chip: the enormous L3 pool means the processor finds the game data it needs without waiting on system memory, which is where frame time actually gets lost. For an RTX 5070 build this is a well-matched pairing. Eight cores is comfortably enough for any current game plus a browser, a chat client and a stream overlay, and the cache advantage lands precisely in the CPU-sensitive titles where a 5070 owner would otherwise see dips. It is also an AM5 part, which means the platform continues forward rather than ending here. The retail box does not include a cooler, but at the time of writing the product page carries a limited-time offer that includes a Cooler Master Elite Liquid 240 AIO with purchase, plus a 4% off coupon in the buy box, which softens that cost considerably. Contender 2: Ryzen 5 9600X, $199.99 The Ryzen 5 9600X is the budget answer: a Zen 5 chip with 6 cores and 12 threads, boosting to 5.4 GHz, at a genuinely low 65W. It is a newer architecture than the 7700X3D and it is $129 cheaper, and in plenty of games paired with a 5070 you will not feel the difference. It also runs cool enough that a modest cooler is fine, and it currently carries a Newegg promo code for extra savings. Where it gives ground is the two areas that matter most for this specific card: it has 38MB of total cache against the 7700X3D’s 104MB, and six cores rather than eight. If you play cache-sensitive simulation and strategy titles, or you stream while gaming, that gap becomes visible in the one-percent-low frame times that determine whether gameplay feels smooth. As a way to get a 5070 build running for less, it is a solid choice. As the best partner for the card, it is not. Contender 3: Intel Core Ultra 7 265K, $314.98 The Core Ultra 7 265K brings 20 cores, split as 8 performance and 12 efficiency cores, on the LGA1851 platform at a 125W TDP, and it costs $15 less than the 7700X3D. If your workload is genuinely mixed, with heavy video encoding, compilation or rendering alongside gaming, that core count is real value and it will beat the AMD chip in throughput benchmarks. For gaming specifically, the calculus is different. Those 12 efficiency cores do very little for frame rates, and Arrow Lake does not have anything comparable to 3D V-Cache to lean on. You would also be buying into LGA1851 rather than AM5. Choose this chip if productivity is at least half of what the machine does. If it is a gaming PC that occasionally does other things, the extra cores are paying rent on space you are not using. Contender 4: Ryzen 7 7800X3D, $389 The Ryzen 7 7800X3D is the 7700X3D’s older sibling and the interesting comparison, because they share the same 8-core Zen 4 layout, the same 96MB L3 cache and the same 120W TDP. The difference is clock speed: 4.2 GHz base and 5.0 GHz boost versus 4.0 and 4.5. That buys you a modest gaming uplift for $60 more. Whether that is worth it depends on the rest of the build. With an RTX 5070 at 1440p, the graphics card is the limiting factor in most titles, so the higher clocks have less room to express themselves than they would alongside a much faster GPU. If the $60 would otherwise go toward a larger SSD or a better cooler, the 7700X3D is the smarter allocation. If you already have everything else you want and simply prefer the faster chip, the 7800X3D is a perfectly good buy. The Verdict, by Category Best overall match for the RTX 5070: the Ryzen 7 7700X3D at $329. It has the cache that this class of card benefits from, eight cores for streaming and multitasking, a 120W power budget an ordinary tower cooler can handle, and an AM5 socket with life left in it. Best budget pairing: the Ryzen 5 9600X at $199.99, accepting slightly worse frame consistency in demanding titles. Best if you also work: the Core Ultra 7 265K at $314.98. Best if you want a little more gaming headroom: the 7800X3D at $389. Whichever CPU you choose, do not skimp on the board. An AM5 option like the MSI B850 GAMING PLUS WIFI6E at $151.98 gives you DDR5, PCIe 5.0 graphics support and Wi-Fi 6E without overpaying, and you can compare current card prices across the range on Newegg’s RTX 5070 listings . Remember to enable your memory’s EXPO profile once the system is up, because leaving DDR5 at its default speed quietly undoes part of what you paid for. Frequently Asked Questions Answers to the most common questions about choosing a CPU for an RTX 5070. What is the best CPU for an RTX 5070? The Ryzen 7 7700X3D at $329 is the best overall match. Its 104MB of total cache targets exactly the CPU-limited 1440p scenarios where a 5070 build would otherwise lose frame consistency. Is a Ryzen 5 9600X enough for an RTX 5070? Yes for most games, and it saves $129. But with 38MB of cache against the 7700X3D's 104MB and six cores instead of eight, it gives up some frame consistency in simulation and strategy titles or while streaming. Is the 7800X3D worth $60 more than the 7700X3D? Only marginally in an RTX 5070 build. Both have 8 Zen 4 cores and 96MB of L3; the 7800X3D just clocks higher, and at 1440p the graphics card is usually the limit. Does the RTX 5070 need PCIe 5.0? No. The card supports PCIe 5.0 but works fine in a PCIe 4.0 slot. Any current AM5 board gives you the bandwidth it needs.

title: 5 Best unitQ Alternatives for Product and Customer Feedback Analytics
summary: The best unitQ alternatives for product and customer feedback analytics: Thematic, Enterpret, Chattermill, Productboard, and Pendo compared.
body_text: unitQ is a strong fit for teams that treat customer feedback as a real-time quality signal. It now sells as AI for quality across six modules, covering feedback monitoring, business impact, competitive benchmarking, support quality assurance (QA), AI-moderated interviews, and social. Teams look for alternatives when that surface area is wider than they need, when they want a theme taxonomy they can inspect and edit rather than a scored feed, or when the buyer is a CX and insights function rather than a product quality function. The best unitQ alternative for enterprise CX and insights teams is Thematic, when the priority is quantifying which themes moved a score and being able to show your work. Thematic builds a two-level theme taxonomy from the feedback itself. Every theme traces back to the exact comments that created it. Other tools fit other situations. Enterpret suits product-led teams that want feedback tied to individual accounts, and Chattermill suits high-volume multilingual feedback across business units. Productboard suits teams whose real problem is feedback-to-roadmap prioritization. Pendo suits teams who need behavioral product analytics alongside what users say. Below is the shortlist, where each one genuinely wins, and the trade-off to weigh before signing anything. The list at a glance Thematic : enterprise CX and insights teams that need to quantify what moved a score and defend the answer. Enterpret : product-led teams that want every piece of feedback tied to the customer account behind it. Chattermill : large CX-led brands analyzing high-volume feedback across many languages and business units. Productboard : product teams whose bottleneck is turning feedback into a prioritized roadmap. Pendo : product teams that need in-product behavioral data alongside customer feedback. Here is the same shortlist side by side, with unitQ as the baseline. Tool Best for Main trade-off unitQ Product and quality teams wanting real-time quality signal across many channels Six-module suite is wide; more surface area than a focused analytics layer Thematic Enterprise CX and insights teams needing traceable themes and quantified score impact Built for teams that want to steer the taxonomy, not a hands-off feed Enterpret Product-led teams tying feedback to customer accounts and revenue Enterprise-only, opaque pricing; weeks to configure the model Chattermill High-volume, multilingual feedback across many business units Strong on analysis, lighter on driving the next action Productboard Prioritization and roadmapping, not deep text analysis Analysis depth is lighter than a dedicated feedback analytics platform Pendo Behavioral product analytics plus in-app guidance Answers what users did, less about what they said at scale What unitQ actually does today Any comparison written more than a few months ago will describe unitQ too narrowly, so it is worth stating the current shape of the product before comparing against it. unitQ positions itself as AI for quality: unify every customer signal, turn it into insights, and tie those to your KPIs in real time. It ingests app reviews, surveys, call transcripts, support tickets, social messages, Reddit, and in-app feedback. The platform is organized as six modules: monitorQ turns feedback into real-time insights so problems surface earlier. metricQ connects feedback, behavior, and business data, and ranks opportunities by impact rather than volume. competeQ analyzes public competitor feedback across app stores, reviews, and social to benchmark quality. supportQ automatically scores agent and bot interactions for QA and compliance. interviewQ runs AI-moderated customer interviews at scale. socialQ monitors social conversations and drafts AI replies. That's a broad platform, and the breadth is the point for teams that want one system covering quality end to end. It's also the reason teams shop around. If you need a rigorous analytics layer on feedback you already collect, six modules is a lot of product to buy, learn, and govern. 1. Thematic Thematic is the customer intelligence layer for enterprise CX and insights teams that need to trust and defend their themes. It analyzes unstructured feedback from surveys, support tickets, reviews, and call transcripts. It builds the theme taxonomy from the bottom up, so the structure emerges from the feedback rather than from a template written two years ago. The differentiator against unitQ is quantified score movement plus traceability. Impact analysis shows how many points each theme adds to or costs a score, so a team reports "shipping delays cost 5 points, support improvements gained 4 points" instead of "quality is down." The score change waterfall decomposes a movement between two periods into the specific themes that caused it. Every theme opens onto the exact verbatims behind it. Analysts can add, delete, and merge themes directly. A skeptical executive can interrogate the result rather than take a score on faith. The proof is in how product teams use it. Levels, a US-based health and wellness company whose users wear a bio-sensor that tracks blood glucose, ran a six-question open-ended user experience survey with 2,700 responses through Thematic. That sat alongside its net promoter score (NPS) and customer satisfaction (CSAT) feedback. Its design, product, and engineering teams explored the resulting themes directly rather than waiting on an analyst. As Levels' Chris Jones put it: "With Thematic, we're able to hone in on the specifics of an issue. That's much more actionable for the product and engineers." The pattern holds at enterprise scale. One large grocery retailer ran impact analysis on post-launch feedback arriving from seven channels. Analysis went from 7 days to 5 hours, 91% faster, and surfaced $4.8M in revenue opportunities a manual process would have missed. The most-mentioned issues were not the most damaging, which is the distinction a volume-ranked quality feed is least likely to make for you. Forrester's Total Economic Impact study put Thematic's three-year ROI at 543%, with payback in under six months, using Forrester's standard Total Economic Impact methodology . The trade-off: Thematic is built for teams that care how themes are constructed and want to maintain them. A team that wants a fully hands-off real-time feed with no human review may find that level of control more than they need, and that is a fair reason to stay with unitQ. 2. Enterpret Enterpret is the closest fit for product-led companies that want every piece of feedback connected to the customer account behind it. Its platform is organized around unifying feedback, understanding it, and acting on it, with an adaptive taxonomy that learns each company's product language and a customer context graph that links signals back to accounts. It also ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, so feedback becomes queryable from an AI assistant, and sales intelligence features that surface deal-level signal. For a product-led-growth company where the product is the customer experience, that account-linked view is genuinely useful. The trade-off is setup and commercial fit. Enterpret sells enterprise-only with pricing that is not public, the custom-trained model can take weeks to configure, and reviewers note a learning curve in getting the taxonomy to a reliable reporting state. 3. Chattermill Chattermill is the strongest fit for large, CX-led enterprises processing feedback at high volume across many languages. It unifies surveys, reviews, social, support conversations, and voice, then applies deep-learning aspect-based sentiment analysis to surface the drivers behind an experience. It is built for scale. Chattermill analyzes feedback in more than 100 languages, with automated translation and transcription built in, and connects with more than 65 feedback channels. It carries the security posture global brands require, including SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022. For a team leaving unitQ because feedback volume across regions has outgrown the tool, this is the natural step up. The trade-off is that Chattermill is analytics-oriented by design. It is strong at telling a team what is trending and weaker at driving the next action, so it will surface the theme without filing the ticket. Pricing is custom and quoted after a sales conversation. 4. Productboard Productboard is the right alternative when the real bottleneck is not analyzing feedback but deciding what to build from it. It positions itself as an agentic product management system, with Productboard Spark, an AI agent carrying context across your product and customers. Its use cases run from customer feedback analysis through product roadmapping, customer engagement, product specification, and strategic planning, so feedback feeds directly into prioritization artifacts rather than into a separate insights report. It states 25+ native integrations and SOC 2 verification. The trade-off is analysis depth. Productboard is a prioritization system that ingests feedback, not a text analytics engine. If you need to quantify how much a theme cost your score across hundreds of thousands of comments, pair it with something built for that, or choose differently. 5. Pendo Pendo suits product teams whose gap is behavioral rather than verbatim. It provides product context for applications and, increasingly, for AI agents, surfacing where users struggle and offering in-app guides and campaigns to intervene at the point of friction. The reason it appears on unitQ shortlists is that both aim at product quality. They approach it from opposite directions. Pendo shows what users did, where they dropped off, and which features went unused. unitQ and the feedback analytics tools show what users said about it. The trade-off is straightforward. Pendo isn't a substitute for feedback analysis at scale, and teams that need both usually run a behavioral tool and an analytics layer side by side rather than expecting one to cover the other. How to choose between them The right pick depends on what breaks first for your team. Ask these questions during a demo: Can we see and edit the theme taxonomy? A good answer shows you the themes, lets you merge or split them, and traces each back to the underlying comments. A vague answer means a black box. Can it tell us which themes moved the score, not just which are loudest? Ask for a score change breakdown across two periods. Frequency without impact sends teams to fix the most-mentioned issue rather than the costliest one. Who is the buyer and the daily user? Product quality tools and CX insights tools optimize for different people. Buying the wrong one produces a platform nobody opens. How much platform are we actually buying? If you need one analytics layer and the vendor sells six modules, ask what the entry configuration looks like and what it costs. Will it sit on our existing stack? Confirm it works alongside your survey platform, warehouse, and BI tool without a rip-and-replace. The short version For teams leaving unitQ because they need a defensible analytics layer rather than a broader quality suite, Thematic is the strongest alternative: themes built from your data, quantified impact on the score, and every theme traceable to the comments behind it. Enterpret is the runner-up for product-led teams that need account-level linkage, and Chattermill for high-volume multilingual programs. If your bottleneck is prioritization rather than analysis, look at Productboard instead. The fastest way to decide is to run the same batch of your own feedback through your top two, then ask each vendor to show you exactly how one theme was built and how much of your last score change it explains. If your shortlist reaches past this page, Thematic compares the field against other incumbents in its guides to Enterpret alternatives , Chattermill alternatives , and Qualtrics alternatives .

title: Modern Treasury Adds Physical and Digital Check Payments to Its Unified Payments API
summary: Modern Treasury’s PSP now supports physical and digital checks through one API alongside ACH, wires, RTP, FedNow, push-to-card, and stablecoins. With built-in ledgering and AML controls, businesses can launch faster, cut operational overhead, and reconcile every payment in one place.
body_text: San Francisco, CA — [August 12, 2026] — Modern Treasury today announced that its Payment Service Provider (PSP) now supports payments via physical and digital checks. Rather than integrating a separate check printing vendor or maintaining distinct reconciliation workflows, developers can use a single API to route payments across ACH, wires, RTP, FedNow, push-to-card, stablecoins, physical checks, and digital checks. The result is less operational complexity, faster implementation, and consistent payment tracking across every rail. Payment Rails Don’t Die Modern Treasury's PSP was built on the premise that no single rail can serve every use case. A vendor payment might move fastest over RTP, a payroll disbursement might run on ACH, and a cross-border settlement might move over stablecoins. Checks are no exception. According to the Federal Reserve’s latest data, 9.2 billion checks are used annually, representing $24.45 trillion in volume. Checks remain structurally required across the industries that move the most money — insurance claims and settlements (where checks still account for roughly 55% of disbursements), legal and escrow payments, construction progress billings, real estate disbursements, healthcare reimbursements, enterprise accounts payable, and unclaimed property administration, where state law mandates checks for remittances. Until now, those teams building on modern payment infrastructure have had to bolt on a separate vendor or legacy process just to cover this one rail. What this means for developers With Modern Treasury’s PSP, customers can now: Choose the appropriate payment rail based on recipient preference, speed, cost, or business rules without changing integrations Generate and mail physical checks directly to a recipient's address Send a digital check that recipients can deposit via mobile banking or remote capture, without waiting on the mail Protect every check with automatic stop payments and Positive Pay - no separate fraud workflow required Add custom logos and attachment pages to both physical and digital checks, preserving brand identity across the full disbursement experience Manage payments within the same dashboard, ledger, and compliance controls used for all other payment types Create financial experiences based on recipient preference, cost, or speed, without maintaining separate systems per method This means developers no longer need a second vendor, a separate API, or a manual workaround to support recipients who need a check. Checks become another payment rail that can be selected alongside ACH, RTP, FedNow, push-to-card, wire transfers, and stablecoins using the same API, orchestration layer, ledger, and reconciliation workflows that Modern Treasury has used to move over $600B in payments. "We have a saying at Modern Treasury: payment rails don't die. There's no better example than checks. No matter how the industry evolves, platforms still need the flexibility to let their customers pay and get paid in the ways that work best for them," said Matt Marcus, Co-Founder and CEO of Modern Treasury. "Instant payment rails like RTP, FedNow, push-to-card, and stablecoins are expanding what's possible, but checks remain essential for millions of recipients. Our job is to ensure customers never have to choose between adopting the newest payment technologies and supporting the rails their business still relies on." Check support is available now to Modern Treasury PSP customers. Learn more at moderntreasury.com/products/payments . About Modern Treasury Modern Treasury provides the most trusted infrastructure for global money movement. Trusted by leading enterprises and financial institutions, the platform helps businesses launch and scale payment experiences in days, not months, with best-in-class developer tools and a single API for both fiat and stablecoin transactions. With built-in compliance, ledgering, and reporting, Modern Treasury enables instant, reliable, and scalable money movement for companies of all sizes. Backed by leading investors including Benchmark, Altimeter, and Salesforce Ventures, Modern Treasury has powered over $600 billion in payments for hundreds of organizations. Learn more about Modern Treasury at www.moderntreasury.com .

title: EyePoint Announces Topline Data from LUGANO, the First of Two Pivotal Phase 3 Clinical Trials for DURAVYU™ 2.7mg in Wet AMD
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about EyePoint, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Release Details EyePoint Announces Topline Data from LUGANO, the First of Two Pivotal Phase 3 Clinical Trials for DURAVYU™ 2.7mg in Wet AMD Aug 17, 2026 PDF Version – DURAVYU was non-inferior to on-label aflibercept control (nominal p-value = 0.0096) in an ad hoc analysis excluding a 4% asymmetric cohort (9 of 211 patients) who experienced vision loss (≥ 15 letters) unrelated to wet AMD; primary endpoint not achieved in full dataset, confounded by this asymmetric cohort – – LUGANO demonstrated clinically meaningful results that reinforce DURAVYU’s potential to improve the treatment paradigm in wet AMD, with compelling key secondary endpoints, including reduction in treatment burden, supplement-free rates, favorable safety profile with redosing, and strong anatomic control through Week 56 compared to on-label aflibercept – – 42% reduction in treatment burden achieving superiority versus on-label aflibercept (nominal p-value of <0.0001) – – 76% of DURAVYU patients were supplement-free up to Week 32 – – 54% of DURAVYU patients were supplement-free and 79% received 0 or 1 supplement up to Week 56; pre-specified analysis on change in BCVA in the supplement-free DURAVYU patients showed non-inferiority to supplement-free aflibercept (nominal p-value = 0.0035) – – Topline data from LUCIA, the second pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial in wet AMD, expected in Q4 2026 with potential FDA New Drug Application submission planned for 1H 2027 – – Conference call to discuss the results to be held today at 8:00 a.m. EDT – WATERTOWN, Mass., Aug. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- EyePoint, Inc. (Nasdaq: EYPT), a company committed to developing and commercializing innovative therapeutics to improve the lives of patients with serious retinal diseases, today announced topline results from LUGANO, the first pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial for DURAVYU™ (vorolanib intravitreal insert) for the treatment of wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD). DURAVYU was non-inferior to on-label aflibercept (nominal p-value = 0.0096) in an ad hoc analysis excluding a 4% asymmetric cohort (9 of 211 patients) who experienced vision loss (≥ 15 letters) unrelated to wet AMD. Despite the outperformance in key secondary endpoints, the primary endpoint of change from baseline in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) versus 2 mg aflibercept on-label control was not achieved in the full dataset, confounded by this asymmetric cohort. In contrast, no patients experienced vision loss (≥ 15 letters) unrelated to wet AMD in the aflibercept control arm. In prior reported similar scale pivotal Phase 3 trials, approximately 3-5% of aflibercept patients lost ≥15 letters1, indicating meaningful overperformance of the on-label aflibercept control group in LUGANO that also contributed to the primary endpoint performance. LUGANO demonstrated clinically meaningful results that reinforce DURAVYU’s potential to improve the treatment paradigm in wet AMD, with compelling key secondary endpoints in reduction in treatment burden, supplement-free rates, a favorable safety profile with redosing, and anatomic control through Week 56 compared to on-label aflibercept. These results represent a meaningful improvement to current wet AMD standard of care. “We are pleased to see that DURAVYU provided clinically meaningful results in the LUGANO trial. The outstanding outcomes across key secondary endpoints, paired with visual improvement, reinforce our confidence in DURAVYU’s potential to transform the current wet AMD treatment paradigm,” said Jay S. Duker, M.D., President and CEO of EyePoint. “While the primary endpoint result for the full dataset was unexpected, the consistently positive results from the pre-specified secondary endpoints and the ad hoc analysis on the primary endpoint present a compelling case for DURAVYU as a new potential therapeutic option for wet AMD. We look forward to a potential New Drug Application (NDA) filing with FDA in the first half of 2027, pending LUCIA results in the fourth quarter of 2026.” Key Secondary Endpoints Across All Patients Key secondary endpoints including a favorable safety profile, reduction in treatment burden, supplement-free rates, and anatomic controls were achieved. Favorable Safety Profile DURAVYU observed to be safe and well tolerated with repeat dosing in patients No difference in cataracts, elevated intraocular pressure, or intraocular inflammation between study and control group No observed occurrences of insert migration, anterior chamber opacities, free-floating drug particles, retinal vasculitis, or severe intraocular inflammation (IOI) Reduction in Treatment Burden 42% reduction in treatment burden, achieving superiority versus on-label aflibercept (nominal p-value<0.0001) compared to a maximum possible reduction of 60% This reduction translates to two fewer injections on average in DURAVYU patients versus on-label aflibercept up to Week 56 Supplement-Free Rates 76% of DURAVYU patients were supplement-free up to Week 32 94 % of DURAVYU patients received zero or one supplement up to Week 32 54% of DURAVYU patients were supplement-free up to Week 56 79% of DURAVYU patients received zero or one supplement up to Week 56 Pre-specified analysis of change in BCVA from baseline to average Week 52/56 in supplement-free patients showed that DURAVYU was non-inferior (nominal p-value=0.0035) versus on-label aflibercept Anatomic Control Strong anatomic control demonstrated DURAVYU’s potency with a mean difference of 4 microns versus on-label aflibercept control in central subfield thickness (CST) at Week 56 The 54% of DURAVYU eyes that were supplement free up to week 56 showed only a 3-micron difference in CST compared to the on-label aflibercept control “The LUGANO results are clinically meaningful because the trial compared DURAVYU to on-label aflibercept, the current gold standard control group in wet AMD trials. Nearly 80% of DURAVYU-treated patients received one or no supplemental injections through Week 56. Disease control with this degree of durability, coupled with a favorable safety profile, would meaningfully reduce the treatment burden for our patients,” said Carl D. Regillo, M.D., FACS, Former Director of the Wills Eye Hospital Retina Service, Professor of Ophthalmology, Thomas Jefferson University. “DURAVYU's ability to control disease well in the majority of patients with a six-month redosing interval represents a significant advance for our patients with wet AMD. In clinical practice, keeping patients adequately treated over time is a big challenge, and a sustained delivery option with this kind of profile would be a welcome addition to the armamentarium.” “DURAVYU demonstrated durable efficacy results with stable retinal anatomy maintained through Week 56, avoiding the sawtooth pattern commonly seen with intermittent anti-VEGF therapy. In addition, the supplement-free anatomic and visual outcomes further validate the potency of DURAVYU,” said Ramiro Ribeiro, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer of EyePoint. “These findings represent an important advancement for retinal disease treatment, demonstrating the potential for repeat dosing of a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), a capability unique to our clinical program, coupled with a favorable safety profile. We extend our sincere gratitude to the patients, caregivers, and investigators whose partnership and dedication made this study possible.” EyePoint plans to present additional details on the LUGANO dataset, including subgroup-analyses, at major retina conferences in the coming months, beginning at the Retina Society 59th Annual Scientific Meeting from September 23-26, 2026. The Company remains on track to report topline data from the second wet AMD pivotal Phase 3 LUCIA trial in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Company anticipates potentially filing an NDA for DURAVYU for the potential treatment of wet AMD in the first half of 2027. Additionally, the pivotal Phase 3 COMO and CAPRI clinical trials for DURAVYU in diabetic macular edema (DME) rapidly completed enrollment, with topline data for both trials anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2027. Conference Call Information EyePoint management will host a conference call today, August 17, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. EDT to discuss the LUGANO topline results. To access the live conference call and webcast, please register via the Events & Presentations page of the Investors section of the Company website at https://investors.eyepoint.bio/events-and-presentations/events . A webcast replay and the data presentation will also be available on the corporate website at the conclusion of the call. About the Phase 3 Wet AMD Program LUGANO and LUCIA are identical, randomized, double-masked, aflibercept controlled, non-inferiority Phase 3 trials assessing the efficacy and safety of DURAVYU in patients with active wet AMD including both treatment naïve and treatment experienced patients. Enrollment is complete in both trials with over 900 patients enrolled. At Day 1, patients are randomized 1:1 to receive either DURAVYU 2.7mg every six months or on-label aflibercept as control. All active patients in the treatment arm have reached the Week 32 visit, during which patients received their second DURAVYU dose. The LUGANO and LUCIA trials are the only sustained release wet AMD pivotal Phase 3 trials evaluating 6-month redosing in both trials over two years. DURAVYU is delivered via a standard intravitreal injection in the physician's office, similar to current practice with FDA approved anti-VEGF treatments. The primary endpoint of the Phase 3 pivotal trials is non-inferiority in the average change in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at weeks 52 and 56 compared to baseline. Secondary endpoints include safety, reduction in treatment burden, percentage of eyes free of supplemental aflibercept injections, and anatomical results as measured by optical coherence tomography (OCT). More information about the trials is available at www.clinicaltrials.gov (LUGANO identifier: NCT06668064; LUCIA identifier: NCT06683742). About Wet AMD Wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD) is a leading cause of vision loss and irreversible blindness in people over the age of fifty. Wet AMD is an advanced form of AMD that develops when abnormal blood vessels grow under the macular retina, leaking blood and/or fluid, and leading to potentially severe vision loss. Wet AMD is a lifelong disease that requires continuous treatment so that patients may maintain visual function. Although multiple treatments are now available, challenges still exist as the current standard-of-care is dosed on average every two months in the United States under a treat-and-extend protocol, and these large molecule anti-VEGF treatments only target one pathology of the disease. This lifetime of frequent treatment represents a tremendous burden for patients, physicians, and the health care system, potentially leading to patient noncompliance and further vision loss. About DURAVYU™ DURAVYU™ (vorolanib intravitreal insert), is an investigational sustained-delivery treatment for patients suffering from serious retinal diseases. DURAVYU combines vorolanib, a selective and patent-protected tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), in next-generation bioerodible Durasert E™, a proprietary and best-in-class IVT delivery technology designed to provide sustained release of drug for at least six months without free-floating drug particles. DURAVYU brings a potential new multi-mechanism of action and treatment paradigm for retinal diseases beyond existing anti-VEGF large molecule ligand blocking therapies, as vorolanib acts intracellularly to suppress angiogenesis through the inhibition of all VEGF receptors and PDGFR, while also suppressing inflammation through the inhibition of interleukin 6 (IL-6)/JAK1 signaling. In addition to the safety and efficacy results demonstrated in the DAVIO, DAVIO 2 and VERONA clinical trials, vorolanib has also demonstrated neuroprotection in an in-vivo model of retinal detachment. DURAVYU has established safety and efficacy data from both Phase 1 and 2 trials in wet AMD and DME that demonstrate stability in vision and anatomical control with a single dose of DURAVYU. No drug-related safety concerns were observed in over 190 patients across four completed clinical trials, including three Phase 2 trials. Informed by the robust Phase 2, DAVIO trial, which achieved statistically positive and clinically meaningful results vs. on-label aflibercept, the fully enrolled wet AMD Phase 3 pivotal program (LUGANO and LUCIA) is the only investigational program evaluating every six-month dosing of DURAVYU, which enables the potential to support a compelling competitive label and advantage for DURAVYU. With over 900 patients randomized across both trials, the Phase 3 pivotal program follows a well-established regulatory approval pathway with a patient-centric noninferiority design comparing DURAVYU to on-label standard of care to inform real-word treatment practices. LUCIA topline data results are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. DURAVYU is also being evaluated for the treatment of DME, with both Phase 3 trials (COMO and CAPRI) fully enrolled and underway. The Phase 2 VERONA trial in DME met primary and secondary endpoints and demonstrated a rapid and sustained improvement in vision and anatomy and a continued favorable safety and tolerability profile with superior dosing intervals to standard of care. Pivotal data from the Phase 3 DME program is anticipated to be reported in the fourth quarter of 2027. About EyePoint EyePoint, Inc. (Nasdaq: EYPT) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company committed to developing and commercializing innovative therapeutics to improve the lives of patients with serious retinal diseases. The Company’s lead product candidate, DURAVYU™, is an innovative investigational sustained delivery treatment for serious retinal diseases combining vorolanib, a selective and patent-protected tyrosine kinase inhibitor, in next-generation bioerodible Durasert E™ technology. Supported by robust safety and efficacy data across multiple clinical trials and indications, DURAVYU is currently being evaluated in Phase 3 pivotal trials for wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME). The Company is committed to partnering with the retinal community to improve patient lives while creating long-term value, with four approved drugs over three decades and tens of thousands of eyes treated with EyePoint innovation. EyePoint is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts, with a commercial manufacturing facility in Northbridge, Massachusetts. Vorolanib is licensed to EyePoint exclusively by Equinox Sciences, a Betta Pharmaceuticals affiliate, for the localized treatment of all ophthalmic diseases outside of China, Macao, Hong Kong and Taiwan. DURAVYU ™ has been conditionally accepted by the FDA as the proprietary name for EYP-1901. DURAVYU is an investigational product; it has not been approved by the FDA. FDA approval and the timeline for potential approval is uncertain.
